chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Ajlan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman performing Tamattu' arrived in Mecca and saw blood (menstruation); what should she do? He said: 'She runs between As-Safa and Al-Marwah and sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf around the House. If she does not become pure, then when it is the Day of Tarwiyah, she pours water over herself, enters the state of Ihram for Hajj with the Talbiyah, and goes out to Mina. She completes all the rituals. When she does that, everything becomes lawful for her except the bed of her husband.'

He said: And I and Ubaydullah ibn Salih heard this Hadith in the mosque. Ubaydullah entered upon Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and then came out to me and said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the narration of Ajlan, and he narrated to me something similar to what we heard from Ajlan.

With Hajj, without that being a mandatory obligation. The second aspect is that it is not explicit in both narrations that she saw blood in any state. And if that is not explicit in their apparent meaning, it is permissible that the meaning intended by both is that she saw blood after she performed Tawaf from the obligatory Tawaf, more than half. For if the matter is as we mentioned, she is in the position of one who has completed her Tamattu'. And that which indicates what we mentioned is what they narrated:

key_terms.أَهَلَّتْ بِالْحَجِّ: Entered the state of Ihram for Hajj with Talbiyah
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.مُتَمَّتَةٌ: A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she starts her Hajj al-Tamattu' while menstruating?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific procedure for a woman in Hajj al-Tamattu' who begins her pilgrimage while menstruating, emphasizing that she completes the Sa'i and waits for purity to perform Tawaf al-Ziyarah. If menstruation persists until the Day of Tarwiyah, she performs Ghusl, enters Ihram for Hajj, and completes the remaining rituals, thereby validating her Tamattu' and permitting all marital relations except sexual intercourse. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the validity of the pilgrimage acts and the specific prohibition of sexual intimacy during the state of Ihram.
